purpose: Tofacitinib is used to treat certain types of arthritis, including rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis. It is also used for ulcerative colitis, a type of inflammatory bowel disease. It helps reduce pain, swelling, and stiffness by calming down an overactive immune system.
how_it_works: Your immune system uses special proteins called JAK enzymes to send signals that cause inflammation. Tofacitinib blocks these JAK enzymes, which helps turn down the inflammation that causes your symptoms. Think of it like turning down the volume on the signals that are making your body attack itself.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections like the common cold or sinus infections, headache, diarrhea, stuffy or runny nose, and stomach upset. Some people may also notice elevated cholesterol levels, so your doctor will monitor your blood work regularly.
warnings: This medication can lower your immune system, making it harder to fight infections, including serious ones like tuberculosis, pneumonia, and fungal infections. There is also an increased risk of blood clots, serious heart events, and certain cancers including lymphoma. It is not recommended if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to monitor your safety while on this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for rheumatoid arthritis is 5 mg taken by mouth twice a day, or 11 mg of the extended-release tablet (Xeljanz XR) once a day. For ulcerative colitis, the starting dose may be higher at first and then reduced. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, with or without food.
